text:
Apple’s sales warning puts pressure on the European luxury market By 0 75
The European luxury market is taking a tumble in Thursday trading after Apple Inc.’s sales forecast cut ramped up concerns about the Chinese market for high-end goods.
Apple AAPL, +4.27% now expects first-quarter revenue of $84 billion, below previous expectations of $89 billion to $93 billion. The FactSet consensus is for sales of $85.47 billion. Apple is scheduled to report first-quarter earnings on Jan. 29.
London’s FTSE 100 index UKX, +2.16% took a tumble on Thursday following Apple’s announcement, and closed down 0.4%. Burberry Group PLC BRBY, +4.59% shares were down nearly 6% in Thursday trading while Kering KER, +4.39% whose brands include Gucci and Yves Saint Laurent, was down 5.5%, LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE LVMH, +3.07% was down 3.6% and Christian Dior SE CDI, +2.67% is off 2.3%.
See: Apple cut holiday sales forecast on iPhone and China weakness, stock falls 8%
“China is by far the most important player in the global luxury goods market with wealthy Chinese buying around $120 billion of high-end goods per year accounting for about a third of the global demand,” wrote Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at City Index by Gain Capital, a specialist in spread betting FX and CFD trading.
“But the ongoing friction with the U.S. is beginning to show its teeth and domestic economic indicators are showing a slowdown in the country’s manufacturing and services sectors, which is only one step from declining consumer demand.”
Concerns about the Chinese luxury market began to grow months ago, with HSBC analysts suggesting four stocks that are most likely to withstand any contraction in the Chinese market: Hugo Boss AG BOSS, +2.49%
